subject: SparrowX-4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice and recovery update
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@northbound.health>; platform@northbound.health
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SparrowX-4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice and recovery update

Hi Alyssa / Northbound platform team,

We observed an elevated rate of 5xx errors and short-duration timeouts for requests routed to model variant "sparrowx-4b" beginning ~2028-06-21T08:45 PDT. The initial spike affected ~3.2% of requests for a 30-minute window and presented as intermittent OOM-style failures and connection resets.

Immediate actions we took:
- Applied an emergency routing rule to divert traffic to sparrowx-4b-fallback (quantized variant) at 08:55 PDT to stabilize customer-facing traffic.
- Kicked off an autoscale warm-up for additional dedicated pools.
- Captured logs and a latency histogram (attached) and opened INC-2028-4321 for tracking.

Why this matters: we know you rely on low tail latency and high success rate for inference in your production Pipelines service. This incident may have caused transient 5xxs in user-facing flows.

Next steps and asks:
- We're collecting a sample of failing requests (attached) — if you have specific request IDs you saw on your side please forward them and we'll correlate.
- We'll follow up with a detailed recovery note and a preliminary root cause within 24 hours.
- If you'd like a bridge, we can stand one up now; otherwise we'll continue async updates.

Attachments: sparrowx-4b-error-sample.log (excerpt), sparrowx-4b-latency-chart-20280621.png, incident-runbook-link.txt

Apologies for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority — I'll send a recovery update as soon as we have it.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SparrowX-4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice and recovery update

Looping infra and runtime here. Quick notes after initial triage:
- Symptoms align with a kernel-selection regression introduced in the 2028-06-20 rollout for sparrowx-4b on CUDA kernels for A100s — under certain context-length distributions the allocator did not reclaim KV cache segments fast enough, producing intermittent OOMs.
- Temporary mitigations in-flight: enable aggressive KV eviction on affected pools; revert kernel selection flag on canary hosts; keep fallback routing to quantized variant for public traffic.
- Charging infra to validate an ordered rollback path and prepare canary validation steps.

I'll coordinate a KB rollback if we see reoccurrence after mitigations. Monica — can you confirm whether Dedicated pools for Northbound were on the affected flag?

Ben
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@northbound.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: SparrowX-4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — recovery update and next steps

Alyssa — quick recovery summary and follow-up items.

What happened (preliminary):
- Root cause: an incorrect kernel selection heuristic pushed a performance-optimized kernel onto a subset of A100 hosts. Under typical request context distributions for sparrowx-4b this kernel produced poor KV cache reclamation behavior, leading to transient memory pressure and downstream 5xxs/timeouts.
- Impact window: ~2028-06-21T08:45–09:20 PDT; affected ~3.2% of requests for sparrowx-4b in that window.

What we did: 
- Diverted customer traffic to sparrowx-4b-fallback at 08:55 PDT (no code changes required) — this restored normal success rates for your traffic within ~5 minutes.
- Reverted the kernel-selection flag on affected canaries and enabled aggressive KV eviction on the affected pools.
- Added an automated check in our deployment gating to detect similar allocator regressions.

Current status:
- Production traffic for your account has been stable since 09:00 PDT on 2028-06-21.
- We will run a controlled canary and validation (including your production-like test set) before re-enabling the optimized kernel. Expect that canary tomorrow morning Pacific.

Compensation and follow-up:
- We will open a formal postmortem and share action items and timelines by 2028-06-24.
- If this incident caused measurable client impact for Northbound, we are prepared to discuss a one-time service credit; I'll coordinate with finance once we have confirmed the impact window.

Attachments and references: incident-runbook-link.txt (contains the runbook + incident ticket INC-2028-4321), charts showing latency/5xx windows (attached).

If you prefer a short post-incident bridge with our engineering leads, we can schedule one — available windows Monday 09:00–11:00 PDT.

Thanks for the quick coordination and for pulling your logs — that made correlation faster.

Best regards,
Logan Wright
Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
